edges.description: Mannose-binding adhesion localizes the trophozoite to the corneal epithelium and initiates contact-dependent epithelial cell damage.
Acanthamoeba proteases and epithelial cytolysis allow organisms to cross the epithelial barrier and digest extracellular matrix in the stroma.
Stromal invasion localizes organisms and inflammation deeper in the cornea, including along stromal nerves.
Stromal Acanthamoeba infection stimulates corneal epithelial cytokine release and a granulocytic inflammatory response.

edges.description: Corneal inflammation is the defining clinical manifestation.
Acanthamoeba perineuritis and keratitis produce severe ocular pain.
Inflammatory keratitis and anterior-segment irritation make light exposure painful.
Stromal inflammation, infiltration, and scarring reduce corneal transparency and visual acuity.
Perineural stromal inflammation produces the radial keratoneuritis sign of Acanthamoeba keratitis.
Anterior-segment inflammation manifests clinically as ocular redness.
Irritative keratitis and ocular pain increase tearing.
The exposure route places Acanthamoeba organisms at the corneal surface where trophozoites can bind mannosylated epithelial glycoproteins.
